text:
Good afternoon on this Sunday. First, the news from home.

Story one: The National Democratic Congress has been conducting its constituency executive elections across the country. According to reports from MyJoyOnline, 3News, and The Ghana Report, all twenty-four executive positions in Juaboso went unopposed, while police in Bimbilla arrested delegates for taking photographs of their ballots, and party leaders promised to investigate any evidence of vote-buying.

Story two: President John Dramani Mahama has called for a new regional security accord at the Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Ethiopia. Graphic Online and 3News report that the president urged West African nations to boost security cooperation, protect economic sovereignty, and prevent Africa from becoming a battleground for global rivalries.

Story three: The Coalition Against Galamsey has petitioned the Attorney-General to investigate GoldBod Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi over comments alleged to encourage unlicensed mining. 3News reports that GoldBod has rejected the accusation, stating that a viral video misrepresents Mr Gyamfi's remarks during consultations on a small-scale mining support scheme.

Now, around the world.

Story four: Voters in Brazil are casting their ballots today in a tightly contested presidential runoff election. The BBC, The Guardian, and France twenty-four report that leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is seeking re-election against far-right challenger Flávio Bolsonaro after a tense campaign.

Story five: France has seen widespread protests over the rising cost of living, leading to more than one thousand three hundred arrests across the country. BBC News and France twenty-four report that while hundreds of thousands marched peacefully, clashes erupted between security forces and demonstrators in several major cities.

You can open Dad News and ask for more about any story by its number.
